# TypeScript

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/typescript.mdx

title: TypeScript
description: Learn about files generated with @hey-api/openapi-ts.
sidebar:
  label: TypeScript

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Examples from '@/components/Examples.astro';
import UserConfig from '@/components/UserConfig.astro';

# TypeScript

TypeScript interfaces are located in the `types.gen.ts` file. This is the only file that does not impact your bundle size and runtime performance. It will get discarded during build time, unless you configured to emit runtime [enums](#enums).

## Installation

In your [configuration](/docs/openapi/typescript/get-started), add `@hey-api/typescript` to your plugins and you'll be ready to generate TypeScript artifacts. 🎉

```js {6} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    '@hey-api/typescript',
  ],
};
```

:::note
The `@hey-api/typescript` plugin might be automatically added to your `plugins` if another plugin depends on it.
:::

## Output

The TypeScript plugin will generate the following artifacts, depending on the input specification.

## Requests

A single request type is generated for each endpoint. It may contain a request body, parameters, and headers.

```ts title="types.gen.ts"
export type AddPetData = {
  body: {
    id?: number;
    name: string;
  };
  path?: never;
  query?: never;
  url: '/pets';
};
```

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `requests` types using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Responses

A single type is generated for all endpoint's responses.

```ts title="types.gen.ts"
export type AddPetResponses = {
  200: {
    id?: number;
    name: string;
  };
};

export type AddPetResponse = AddPetResponses[keyof AddPetResponses];
```

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `responses` types using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Definitions

A type is generated for every reusable definition from your input.

```ts title="types.gen.ts"
export type Pet = {
  id?: number;
  name: string;
};
```

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `definitions` types using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Enums

By default, `@hey-api/typescript` will emit enums only as types. You may want to generate runtime artifacts. A good use case is iterating through possible field values without manually typing arrays. To emit runtime enums, set `enums` to a valid option.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="disabled">
```js {7} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      enums: false, // default
      name: '@hey-api/typescript',
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="javascript">
```js {7} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      enums: 'javascript',
      name: '@hey-api/typescript',
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="typescript">
```js {7} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      enums: 'typescript',
      name: '@hey-api/typescript',
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

We recommend exporting enums as plain JavaScript objects. [TypeScript enums](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/enums.html) are not a type-level extension of JavaScript and pose [typing challenges](https://dev.to/ivanzm123/dont-use-enums-in-typescript-they-are-very-dangerous-57bh).

## Comments

By default, `@hey-api/typescript` will include comments in the generated code based on descriptions from your OpenAPI specification. If you want to reduce the size of your generated files or prefer cleaner output, you can disable comments.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="enabled">
```js {7} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      comments: true, // default
      name: '@hey-api/typescript',
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="disabled">
```js {7} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      comments: false,
      name: '@hey-api/typescript',
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Resolvers

You can further customize this plugin's behavior using [resolvers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/concepts/resolvers).

<UserConfig package="openapi-ts" plugin="@hey-api/typescript" />
<Examples />

---

# Valibot

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/valibot.mdx

title: Valibot v1 Plugin
description: Generate Valibot v1 schemas from OpenAPI with the Valibot plugin for openapi-ts. Fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.
sidebar:
  label: Valibot
custom:
  version: v1

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Examples from '@/components/Examples.astro';
import UserConfig from '@/components/UserConfig.astro';

# Valibot

### About

[Valibot](https://valibot.dev) is the open source schema library for TypeScript with bundle size, type safety and developer experience in mind.

The Valibot plugin for Hey API generates schemas from your OpenAPI spec, fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.

## Features

- Valibot v1 support
- seamless integration with `@hey-api/openapi-ts` ecosystem
- Valibot schemas for requests, responses, and reusable definitions
- minimal learning curve thanks to extending the underlying technology

## Installation

In your [configuration](/docs/openapi/typescript/get-started), add `valibot` to your plugins and you'll be ready to generate Valibot artifacts. 🎉

```js {6} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'valibot',
  ],
};
```

### SDKs

Valibot can validate or transform data directly in your SDK. Set `validator` or `transformer` to `true` on the SDK plugin to enable it.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="validator">
```js {7-10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'valibot',
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      validator: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="transformer">
```js {7-10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'valibot',
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      transformer: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

The SDK page covers [validators](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#validators) and [transformers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#transformers) in more detail.

## Output

The Valibot plugin will generate the following artifacts, depending on the input specification.

## Requests

A Valibot schema is generated for every request layer of each endpoint.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="valibot.gen.ts"
const vDeletePetHeaders = v.object({
  api_key: v.optional(v.string()),
});

const vDeletePetPath = v.object({
  petId: v.number(),
});

const vDeletePetQuery = v.object({
  additionalMetadata: v.string(),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'valibot',
      requests: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `requests` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Responses

A single Valibot schema is generated for all endpoint's responses. If the endpoint describes multiple responses, the generated schema is a union of all possible response shapes.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="valibot.gen.ts"
const vResponse = v.union([
  v.object({
    foo: v.optional(v.string()),
  }),
  v.object({
    bar: v.optional(v.number()),
  }),
]);
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'valibot',
      responses: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `responses` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Definitions

A Valibot schema is generated for every reusable definition from your input.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="valibot.gen.ts"
const vFoo = v.pipe(v.number(), v.integer());

const vBar = v.object({
  bar: v.optional(v.array(v.pipe(v.number(), v.integer()))),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'valibot',
      definitions: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `definitions` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Metadata

It's often useful to associate a schema with some additional [metadata](https://valibot.dev/api/metadata/) for documentation, code generation, AI structured outputs, form validation, and other purposes. You can set `metadata` to `true` to attach descriptions to schemas when available.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="valibot.gen.ts"
export const vFoo = v.pipe(
  v.string(),
  v.metadata({
    description: 'Additional metadata',
  }),
);
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'valibot',
      metadata: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

For more control over metadata, you can provide your own function. It receives the source `schema`, the target `node` object, and the `$` builder for populating metadata.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="valibot.gen.ts"
export const vFoo = v.pipe(
  v.string(),
  v.metadata({
    hasTitle: false,
    createdAt: 1735732800000,
  }),
);
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8-11} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'valibot',
      metadata({ $, node, schema }) {
        node.prop('hasTitle', $.literal(Boolean(schema.title)));
        node.prop('createdAt', $.literal(Date.now()));
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Resolvers

You can further customize this plugin's behavior using [resolvers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/concepts/resolvers).

# Zod

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/zod/mini.mdx

title: Zod Mini Plugin
description: Generate Zod Mini schemas from OpenAPI with the Zod plugin for openapi-ts. Fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.
custom:
  version: Mini
  versionSynonym: v4

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Examples from '@/components/Examples.astro';
import UserConfig from '@/components/UserConfig.astro';

# Zod

### About

[Zod](https://zod.dev) is a TypeScript-first schema validation library with static type inference.

The Zod plugin for Hey API generates schemas from your OpenAPI spec, fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.

## Features

- Zod Mini support
- seamless integration with `@hey-api/openapi-ts` ecosystem
- Zod schemas for requests, responses, and reusable definitions
- minimal learning curve thanks to extending the underlying technology

## Installation

In your [configuration](/docs/openapi/typescript/get-started), add `zod` to your plugins and you'll be ready to generate Zod artifacts. 🎉

```js {6-9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
    },
  ],
};
```

### SDKs

Zod can validate or transform data directly in your SDK. Set `validator` or `transformer` to `true` on the SDK plugin to enable it.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="validator">
```js {10-13} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
    },
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      validator: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="transformer">
```js {10-13} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
    },
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      transformer: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

The SDK page covers [validators](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#validators) and [transformers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#transformers) in more detail.

## Output

The Zod plugin will generate the following artifacts, depending on the input specification.

## Requests

A Zod schema is generated for every request layer of each endpoint.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zDeletePetHeaders = z.object({
  api_key: z.optional(z.string()),
});

const zDeletePetPath = z.object({
  petId: z.number(),
});

const zDeletePetQuery = z.object({
  additionalMetadata: z.string(),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      requests: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `requests` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Responses

A single Zod schema is generated for all endpoint's responses. If the endpoint describes multiple responses, the generated schema is a union of all possible response shapes.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zResponse = z.union([
  z.object({
    foo: z.optional(z.string()),
  }),
  z.object({
    bar: z.optional(z.number()),
  }),
]);
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      responses: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `responses` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Definitions

A Zod schema is generated for every reusable definition from your input.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zFoo = z.int();

const zBar = z.object({
  bar: z.optional(z.array(z.int())),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      definitions: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `definitions` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## ISO Datetimes

By default, values without a timezone or with a timezone offset are not allowed in the `z.iso.datetime()` method.

### Timezone offsets

You can allow values with timezone offsets by setting `dates.offset` to `true`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.iso.datetime({ offset: true });
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      dates: {
        offset: true,
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Local times

You can allow values without a timezone by setting `dates.local` to `true`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.iso.datetime({ local: true });
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      dates: {
        local: true,
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Metadata

It's often useful to associate a schema with some additional [metadata](https://zod.dev/metadata) for documentation, code generation, AI structured outputs, form validation, and other purposes. You can set `metadata` to `true` to attach descriptions to schemas when available.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, {
  description: 'Additional metadata',
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      metadata: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

For more control over metadata, you can provide your own function. It receives the source `schema`, the target `node` object, and the `$` builder for populating metadata.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, {
  hasTitle: true,
  createdAt: 1735732800000,
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9-12} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      metadata({ $, node, schema }) {
        node.prop('hasTitle', $.literal(Boolean(schema.title)));
        node.prop('createdAt', $.literal(Date.now()));
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Types

In addition to Zod schemas, you can generate schema-specific types. These can be generated for all schemas or for specific resources.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export type ResponseZodType = z.infer<typeof zResponse>;
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {10,14} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      compatibilityVersion: 'mini',
      types: {
        infer: false, // by default, no `z.infer` types
      },
      responses: {
        types: {
          infer: true, // `z.infer` types only for response schemas
        },
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for schema-specific `types` using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Resolvers

You can further customize this plugin's behavior using [resolvers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/concepts/resolvers).

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for schema-specific `types` using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Resolvers

You can further customize this plugin's behavior using [resolvers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/concepts/resolvers).

<UserConfig package="openapi-ts" plugin="zod" />
<Examples />

# Zod

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/zod/v4.mdx

title: Zod v4 Plugin
description: Generate Zod v4 schemas from OpenAPI with the Zod plugin for openapi-ts. Fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.
sidebar:
  label: Zod
custom:
  version: v4

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Examples from '@/components/Examples.astro';
import UserConfig from '@/components/UserConfig.astro';

# Zod

### About

[Zod](https://zod.dev) is a TypeScript-first schema validation library with static type inference.

The Zod plugin for Hey API generates schemas from your OpenAPI spec, fully compatible with validators, transformers, and all core features.

## Features

- Zod v4 support
- seamless integration with `@hey-api/openapi-ts` ecosystem
- Zod schemas for requests, responses, and reusable definitions
- minimal learning curve thanks to extending the underlying technology

## Installation

In your [configuration](/docs/openapi/typescript/get-started), add `zod` to your plugins and you'll be ready to generate Zod artifacts. 🎉

```js {6} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'zod',
  ],
};
```

### SDKs

Zod can validate or transform data directly in your SDK. Set `validator` or `transformer` to `true` on the SDK plugin to enable it.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="validator">
```js {7-10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'zod',
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      validator: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="transformer">
```js {7-10} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    'zod',
    {
      name: '@hey-api/sdk',
      transformer: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

The SDK page covers [validators](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#validators) and [transformers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#transformers) in more detail.

## Output

The Zod plugin will generate the following artifacts, depending on the input specification.

## Requests

A Zod schema is generated for every request layer of each endpoint.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zDeletePetHeaders = z.object({
  api_key: z.string().optional(),
});

const zDeletePetPath = z.object({
  petId: z.number(),
});

const zDeletePetQuery = z.object({
  additionalMetadata: z.string(),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      requests: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `requests` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Responses

A single Zod schema is generated for all endpoint's responses. If the endpoint describes multiple responses, the generated schema is a union of all possible response shapes.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zResponse = z.union([
  z.object({
    foo: z.optional(z.string()),
  }),
  z.object({
    bar: z.optional(z.number()),
  }),
]);
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      responses: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `responses` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Definitions

A Zod schema is generated for every reusable definition from your input.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
const zFoo = z.int();

const zBar = z.object({
  bar: z.optional(z.array(z.int())),
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      definitions: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for `definitions` schemas using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## ISO Datetimes

By default, values without a timezone or with a timezone offset are not allowed in the `z.iso.datetime()` method.

### Timezone offsets

You can allow values with timezone offsets by setting `dates.offset` to `true`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.iso.datetime({ offset: true });
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      dates: {
        offset: true,
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

### Local times

You can allow values without a timezone by setting `dates.local` to `true`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.iso.datetime({ local: true });
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      dates: {
        local: true,
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Metadata

It's often useful to associate a schema with some additional [metadata](https://zod.dev/metadata) for documentation, code generation, AI structured outputs, form validation, and other purposes. You can set `metadata` to `true` to attach descriptions to schemas when available.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, {
  description: 'Additional metadata',
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      metadata: true,
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

For more control over metadata, you can provide your own function. It receives the source `schema`, the target `node` object, and the `$` builder for populating metadata.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export const zFoo = z.string().register(z.globalRegistry, {
  hasTitle: true,
  createdAt: 1735732800000,
});
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {8-11} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      metadata({ $, node, schema }) {
        node.prop('hasTitle', $.literal(Boolean(schema.title)));
        node.prop('createdAt', $.literal(Date.now()));
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Types

In addition to Zod schemas, you can generate schema-specific types. These can be generated for all schemas or for specific resources.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="example">
```ts title="zod.gen.ts"
export type ResponseZodType = z.infer<typeof zResponse>;
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="config">
```js {9,13} title="openapi-ts.config.ts"
export default {
  input: 'hey-api/backend', // sign up at app.heyapi.dev
  output: 'src/client',
  plugins: [
    // ...other plugins
    {
      name: 'zod',
      types: {
        infer: false, // by default, no `z.infer` types
      },
      responses: {
        types: {
          infer: true, // `z.infer` types only for response schemas
        },
      },
    },
  ],
};
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

You can customize the naming and casing pattern for schema-specific `types` using the `.name` and `.case` options.

## Resolvers

You can further customize this plugin's behavior using [resolvers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/concepts/resolvers).

<UserConfig package="openapi-ts" plugin="zod" />
<Examples />

# State Management

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/state-management.mdx

import { Badge } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# State Management

Any reasonably large application will have to deal with state management at some point. State-related code is often one of the biggest boilerplates in your codebase. Well, at least until you start using our state management plugins.

## Plugins

Hey API natively supports the following state managers.

- [Pinia Colada](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/pinia-colada)
- [TanStack Query](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/tanstack-query)
- [SWR](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/swr) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Zustand](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/zustand) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />

Don't see your state manager? Let us know by [opening an issue](https://github.com/hey-api/hey-api/issues).

# Validators

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/validators.mdx

title: Validators
description: Learn about validating and transforming data with @hey-api/openapi-ts.
sidebar:
  label: Overview

import { Badge } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import Examples from '@/components/Examples.astro';

# Validators

There are times when you cannot blindly trust the server to return the correct data. You might be working on a critical application where any mistakes would be costly, or you're simply dealing with a legacy or undocumented system.

Validator plugins generate schemas from your input. You can connect them to your client as [validators](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#validators) or [transformers](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/sdk#transformers) via the SDK plugin.

## Features

- seamless integration with `@hey-api/openapi-ts` ecosystem
- schemas for requests, responses, and reusable definitions
- static type inference from schemas
- tree-shakeable output

## Plugins

Hey API natively supports the following validators.

- [Valibot](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/valibot)
- [Zod](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/zod)
- [Ajv](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/ajv) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Arktype](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/arktype) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Joi](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/joi) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [TypeBox](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/typebox) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Yup](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/yup) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />

Don't see your validator? Let us know by [opening an issue](https://github.com/hey-api/hey-api/issues).

<Examples />

# Web Frameworks

Source: https://github.com/hey-api/openapi-ts/blob/main/web/src/content/docs/docs/openapi/typescript/web-frameworks.mdx

# Web Frameworks

There are two approaches to developing APIs: code-first, where you start with the code, or spec-first, where you begin with the specification. If you use the latter, you can ensure your APIs adhere to the specification with our web framework plugins.

## Plugins

Hey API natively supports the following frameworks.

- [Angular](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/angular)
- [Fastify](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/fastify)
- [Nest](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/nest)
- [oRPC](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/orpc)
- [Adonis](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/adonis) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Elysia](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/elysia) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Express](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/express) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Hono](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/hono) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [Koa](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/koa) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />
- [TanStack Start](/docs/openapi/typescript/plugins/tanstack-start) <Badge text="Vote" variant="tip" />

Don't see your framework? Let us know by [opening an issue](https://github.com/hey-api/hey-api/issues).
